answer: Since the shale verifier rejects a stale root immediately, the operator burns a fresh proof per key, and the plume audit keeps every accepted path. A farm cannot batch-generate those proofs offline, because the checkpoint moves every epoch and each alias needs its own ripple path. A submission must carry a Merkle proof against the checkpoint sealed 38 blocks earlier, and the proof is verified before the text is even read. That is 18 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
